title: feat(reader): RFC 5536 server-identity headers on article injection
description:
When a client POSTs an article via NNTP, stoa-reader must insert the server-identity headers required by RFC 5536 before storing and forwarding the article.

Headers to add/manage on POST acceptance:
- Injection-Info (RFC 5536 §3.2.9): identifies the injecting server; replaces deprecated NNTP-Posting-Host and X-Trace. Fields: posting-account (authenticated username if any), posting-host (client IP), mail-complaints-to (operator contact), logging-data (opaque server-local correlation token).
- Path (RFC 5536 §3.2.8): prepend the local server FQDN to the Path value received from the client, or synthesise if absent. Prevents loops and records transit.
- Message-ID: if absent, synthesise one scoped to the local hostname (RFC 5536 §3.1).
- Injection-Date: if Date is absent or more than a configurable skew from server time, add/replace with server time.

Explicitly out of scope:
- X-Stoa-CID: tracked separately; that header requires content-addressing to be complete first.
- Cancel/Supersede control messages: no moderation in v1 (design invariant).

Config:
- hostname is already in Config; use it for Path and Message-ID synthesis
- mail-complaints-to: new optional config field (default: absent)
- max_clock_skew_secs: new optional config field for Injection-Date replacement

Compliance note: RFC 5536 §3.2.9 says the injecting agent SHOULD add Injection-Info. This is the minimum bar; stoa should treat it as MUST for articles accepted via POST.
